newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police question Timorese who left Austrian mission.
newsitem.headline: Police question Timorese who left Austrian mission.

text.p: Indonesian police questioned 33 East Timorese youths on Thursday after they ended a two-day stay in the Austrian embassy and sent representatives to meet visiting U.N. official Jamsheed Marker.
"They were brought in this morning and they are all still here," a policewoman at police headquarters told Reuters.
"They are still being questioned. I do not know when they will be released," the policewoman, who did not identify herself, said. She declined to provide any further details.

The youths entered the embassy compound on Tuesday afternoon and demanded to meet Marker, the U.N. secretary-general's special envoy on East Timor who is in Jakarta as a part of a familiarisation trip to Indonesia and East Timor.
Only hours after the break-in, three of the youths were taken to meet Marker at United Nations offices in Jakarta.
Austria's ambassador, Hans Demel, told Reuters earlier the 33 youths had left his embassy compound at 5.00 a.m. (2200 GMT).

"Everything went peacefully and in a humanitarian way. They went out of the embassy and went down the street and they went into a (police) bus. It was the 28th of the embassy cases and it was a routine case," Demel said.

He said the agreement with senior officials of the Indonesian Department of Foreign Affairs stipulated the names of the youths would be taken down and then they would be released as happened after a protest in 1995 at the Dutch embassy.

Police held about 50, mostly East Timorese protesters in the December 1995 incident for 24 hours before they were released. A similiar number who simultaneously entered the Russian embassy were held for the same amount of time.

Indonesia's armed forces spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying on Wednesday that the actions of the youths, who climbed over the embassy's fence, were improper.
About 40 youths staged a counter-protest outside the embassy on Wednesday, denouncing the youths inside, witnesses said.
Since September 1995, 108 East Timorese have entered foreign embassies in Jakarta and asked for political asylum, always granted by Portugal, the former colonial ruler of East Timor.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
